title: Wolf and Thorn
premise: Emrys Villalobos, a mercenary bound to a silent god and hiding in the Thorn Valley where magic cannot follow, has spent a decade burying the war that broke them. When a feral child named Wren arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language of the god who abandoned Emrys—they realize the valley's silence was never sanctuary but a cage built around something buried. Pursued by the usurper Vaelric's inquisitors, Emrys must choose between destroying the child (and their last link to the divine) or carrying Wren to the free cities, where the truth of the god's silence—that it was imprisoned by the usurper's bloodline—could either reignite an ancient war or shatter Vaelric's claim before his armies march. In the end, Emrys sacrifices their own memories of belonging to wake the god, saving the cities but forgetting why they ever fought to survive.
about_author: Sable Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing dead languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who carry too much history and not enough hope.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A routine patrol through the magic-dead Thorn Valley establishes Emrys's exile, their sworn-but-silent god, and the quiet dread of a mercenary waiting for a war that already ended without them. Emotional beat: hollow routine masking grief.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A mud-caked child appears at Emrys's door during a storm, speaking words Emrys hasn't heard since the god went silent: the First Tongue. The child, Wren, cannot—or will not—say where they came from. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys tests Wren's language against half-remembered liturgies and realizes the child speaks the tongue of the god Ossa—fluently, natively, impossibly. Emotional beat: vertigo of a past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Silence Cost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through the child's eyes we see Emrys as a frightening, wounded giant, and glimpse fragments of Wren's flight from burning lowlands. Emotional beat: two survivors circling each other, neither able to trust.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Vaelric's inquisitors reach the valley's edge, asking after 'a stolen relic.' Emrys lies for the first time in ten years and understands the choice has already been made. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of commitment.

chapters.title: The God Who Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A flashback-heavy chapter: how Emrys swore to Ossa, how the god's voice died mid-battle, and how Emrys crawled into the magic-dead valley to escape the silence. Emotional beat: guilt revealed as the true wound.

chapters.title: Bargains with Strangers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys seeks out Maren, an exiled hedge-witch at the valley's border, who confirms Wren carries something alive in their blood—and that inquisitors pay well for such things. Emotional beat: temptation of betrayal, refused.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. An inquisitor scouting party finds the cottage; Emrys kills three men whose faces they almost recognize from the old war. Wren watches. Emotional beat: horror at discovering the killer still lives inside the hermit.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crossing the valley boundary, magic floods back—and Wren begins glowing faintly, singing in their sleep, drawing attention like a beacon. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror of being hunted.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The pair travels through villages gutted by Vaelric's conscription, seeing the usurper's war machine firsthand. Emrys teaches Wren to hide their light. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible in others' ruins.

chapters.title: An Old Comrade's Knife
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the free city of Corvane, Emrys meets Sefa, a former shield-sister now selling information—who offers to sell Wren instead. Their confrontation ends unresolved, a knife between old friends. Emotional beat: betrayal as mirror.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Archive
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following Maren's clues, Emrys breaks into a forbidden archive and learns the truth: Ossa was not silent but imprisoned, sealed beneath Vaelric's citadel by the first usurper's bloodline. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes a decade of abandonment.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finally speaks plainly: they are not a child of Ossa but the god's last fragment, hidden in mortal flesh when the prison was sealed. Emotional beat: devastating innocence carrying unbearable weight.

chapters.title: The Choice of Chains
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys can end it here—kill Wren, keep the peace, keep surviving—or carry the fragment to the god's remaining faithful and risk reigniting the ancient war. Emotional beat: the full weight of the secret, held alone.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Sefa returns with Vaelric's inquisitors behind her—but at the critical moment she turns her blade on them instead, buying Emrys and Wren escape at the cost of her own life. Emotional beat: redemption arriving too late to enjoy.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A running battle across Corvane's rooftops and canals as the faithful smuggle Emrys and Wren toward the old pilgrimage road. Emotional beat: belonging found, briefly, among strangers who share the burden.

chapters.title: The Pilgrimage Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the road to the prison-citadel, Wren grows weaker as the god within stirs, and asks Emrys whether being remembered is worth dying for. Emotional beat: tenderness before catastrophe.

chapters.title: Gates of the Usurper
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys infiltrates Vaelric's citadel during the eve-of-war feast, discovering Vaelric knows exactly what Wren is—and wants the god's power for himself. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into defiance.

chapters.title: The Prison Beneath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the deep vaults, Emrys and Wren find Ossa's prison; Vaelric arrives to claim the god. Wren offers themselves willingly to break the seal. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, at last.

chapters.title: Wolf and Thorn
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax: Emrys holds the vault against Vaelric's guard while Wren dissolves into the waking god. To complete the awakening, Ossa requires a memory of belonging as anchor—and Emrys gives up every memory of the valley, of home, of why they fought. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with self-erasure.

chapters.title: The God Who Speaks Again
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Ossa rises, Vaelric's armies falter as their commander's legitimacy crumbles, and the free cities hold. But Emrys stands amid the victory feeling nothing, knowing only that something precious was paid and cannot be recalled. Emotional beat: hollow victory, grief without object.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reborn in mortal form beside the awakened god, Wren finds Emrys on the valley's edge—a stranger now, but one who still, inexplicably, leaves the door unlatched. Some things outlast memory. Emotional beat: cautious, hard-won hope; belonging beginning again.
